title: Gemini embedding responses lack body and read-time bounds
summary: Gemini embedding responses are fully read, decompressed, and materialized into an unrestricted JSON value before count, numeric-type, and dimension validation. A connected remote service or intermediary can therefore block query or index work or drive substantial transient memory and CPU consumption.

severity.rationale: Remote response control is realistic and explicitly in scope once an ordinary approved operation occurs. Existing controls prevent durable bad vectors but not the availability sink; medium impact plus high likelihood maps to medium.
severity.changeConditions: Severity would rise if the response path can reliably create durable multi-scope outage or corrupt stored vectors; it would fall after effective deadlines and body ceilings precede JSON materialization while the existing semantic checks remain intact.

confidence.rationale: bounded parser/control tests+V10. Exact query/index-to-Gemini-POST-to-into_json-to-late-shape-check source trace. Cargo.lock pins ureq 2.12.1; local primary source shows connect=30s, read/write/overall=None, gzip before unbounded serde_json::from_reader. Two bounded network-free parser tests passed for normal order and wrong-dimension rejection.

taxonomy.category: remote response resource exhaustion / missing deadline (CWE-400, CWE-770)

locations.role: Gemini POST and full JSON materialization

codeEvidence.label: Embedding execution reaches the production client
codeEvidence.explanation: The adopted real execution path dispatches the request to the production `GeminiEmbeddingAdapter` and waits for its response vectors.

codeEvidence.label: Gemini response is fully materialized
codeEvidence.explanation: The authenticated batch request feeds the entire response to unrestricted `into_json()` before any count, numeric, or dimension check.

codeEvidence.label: Semantic checks occur after materialization
codeEvidence.explanation: Count, numeric-type, and dimension validation protect accepted vector integrity, but only after the complete remote JSON tree is already in memory.

codeEvidence.label: Query waits for adapter completion
codeEvidence.explanation: Online query embedding waits for the adapter call; errors fall back to text search only after the unbounded response operation returns or fails.

codeEvidence.label: Configured timeout is not threaded
codeEvidence.explanation: The configuration path leaves adapter HTTP transports unwired, so the documented timeout does not bound a connected peer's response.

rootCause.summary: The production Gemini client performs unrestricted `into_json()` with no effective read/overall deadline or response-body ceiling. Semantic response checks correctly reject invalid vectors, but they execute only after the resource sink, and the configured timeout remains unwired.

remediation: Use a shared Gemini HTTP client with configured read/write/overall deadlines and compressed/decompressed response byte ceilings before JSON materialization; retain count/dimension checks.

validation.summary: Exact query/index-to-Gemini-POST-to-into_json-to-late-shape-check source trace. Cargo.lock pins ureq 2.12.1; local primary source shows connect=30s, read/write/overall=None, gzip before unbounded serde_json::from_reader. Two bounded network-free parser tests passed for normal order and wrong-dimension rejection.
assertions: Cargo.lock pins ureq 2.12.1; local primary source shows connect=30s, read/write/overall=None, gzip before unbounded serde_json::from_reader.
Two bounded network-free parser tests passed for normal order and wrong-dimension rejection.
counterevidence: Connection establishment has a 30-second timeout and the adopted embedding model is fixed.
Query uses one item; index batches at most 32; response count, numeric JSON type, and dimension are checked.
Invalid responses are not persisted; query errors fall back to text and index errors become failed tasks; online activation/authorization is required.
limitations: No loopback delay/body measurement was run under the read-only/no-network constraint; exact code and pinned dependency defaults make this non-material to disposition.
No loopback slow-read or oversized-body measurement was retained; exact memory and timing thresholds remain unmeasured.

attackPath.summary: The operator activates the Gemini embedding adapter and runs an online query or index operation. KCS sends a one-item query or at-most-32-item index batch to the configured remote service. The service, proxy, or intermediary slow-streams or returns an oversized or highly compressed JSON response. KCS fully reads, decompresses, and materializes the response before count, numeric-type, and dimension checks, allowing the remote peer to block the operation or consume substantial transient resources.

reachability.summary: outbound remote embedding request after adapter activation and authorization; no public inbound endpoint
reachability.attacker: KCS uses the victim OS identity and configured Gemini credential; the remote peer controls only response behavior
reachability.entrypoint: The operator activates the Gemini embedding adapter and runs an online query or index operation.
reachability.preconditions: plausible: an approved query or index call reaches a connected malicious or malfunctioning remote peer
reachability.outcome: query/index availability and transient process memory/CPU

impact.why: Remote response control is realistic and explicitly in scope once an ordinary approved operation occurs. Existing controls prevent durable bad vectors but not the availability sink; medium impact plus high likelihood maps to medium.

likelihood.why: An operator-approved Gemini query or indexing request is made. The connected provider, proxy, or intermediary is faulty, compromised, or hostile.

counterevidence: Small request batches and post-parse shape checks bound accepted semantic output, not the body materialized before those checks.
No invalid vectors are persisted and a returned query error degrades to text search.
limitations: No loopback delay/body measurement was run under the read-only/no-network constraint; exact code and pinned dependency defaults make this non-material to disposition.
No loopback slow-read or oversized-body measurement was retained; exact memory and timing thresholds remain unmeasured.

remediationTests: Use a bounded local fake transport to verify configured deadlines and compressed/decompressed response ceilings stop slow or oversized responses.
Retain count, numeric-type, and dimension rejection tests and confirm no invalid vector is persisted after the transport bounds are added.
preventiveControls: post-materialization count, type, and dimension validation
Use a shared Gemini HTTP client with configured read/write/overall deadlines and compressed/decompressed response byte ceilings before JSON materialization; retain count/dimension checks.
